hero.title: The Republic of the Philippines
hero.description: An archipelago of 7,641 islands in Southeast Asia. Home to 117 million Filipinos across 18 regions, 82 provinces, and more than 180 spoken languages. A sovereign democratic republic since 1946.

islands.desc: Across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao — only about 2,000 inhabited.

population.desc: 12th most populous country in the world; median age 25.

area.desc: Roughly the size of Italy, scattered across 1.5M km² of ocean.

languages.desc: Filipino and English are official; Cebuano, Ilocano, Hiligaynon widely used.

overview.title: What is the Philippines
paragraphs: The Philippines is a sovereign island country in Southeast Asia, situated in the western Pacific Ocean. Its 7,641 islands are broadly categorized under three main geographical divisions from north to south: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. The capital is Manila, and the most populous city is nearby Quezon City, both within the National Capital Region on Luzon.

Archaeological evidence suggests that hominins reached the archipelago more than 700,000 years ago. Modern humans arrived at least 47,000 years ago, and by the first millennium CE, the islands hosted sophisticated maritime polities trading across Asia. Spanish colonization began in 1565 and lasted more than three centuries, followed by American rule from 1898 and Japanese occupation during World War II.

Independence was declared on June 12, 1898, and recognized by the United States on July 4, 1946. Today, the Republic of the Philippines is a constitutional democracy with a presidential form of government. Its 1987 Constitution, ratified after the People Power Revolution, enshrines a system of checks and balances among three co-equal branches: the Executive, the Legislature, and the Judiciary.

Filipinos are among the most outwardly mobile people in the world. An estimated 10 million live and work overseas as Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs), whose remittances form a cornerstone of the economy. At home, the country is known for its strong Catholic traditions, vibrant fiestas, hospitality, and a pop culture that fuses Malay, Spanish, American, and Asian influences.

pullquote.body: The Philippines is not one nation on one island — it is a conversation across three thousand of them, conducted in eighty-something languages, and punctuated by monsoons.
pullquote.source: — Essay, Commission on the Filipino Language · 2023

symbols.title: National symbols
symbols.meta: Established by Republic Act 8491 & Presidential Proclamations

flag.label: Flag
flag.title: Pambansang Watawat
flag.desc: Blue for peace, red for courage, white for equality. Sun with eight rays for the first provinces that rose in revolt; three stars for Luzon, Visayas, Mindanao.

anthem.label: National anthem
anthem.title: Lupang Hinirang
anthem.desc: "Chosen Land." Music composed by Julián Felipe (1898); Tagalog lyrics by José Palma, adapted from his Spanish poem "Filipinas."

seal.label: Seal
seal.title: Dakilang Sagisag
seal.desc: The great seal of the Republic bears the sun and three stars of the flag, the official name in Filipino, and is used to authenticate state documents.

bird.label: National bird
bird.title: Pithecophaga jefferyi
bird.desc: One of the world's largest and rarest raptors. Endemic to Mindanao, Luzon, Samar, Leyte. Fewer than 400 breeding pairs remain.

tree.label: National tree
tree.title: Pterocarpus indicus
tree.desc: A tropical hardwood whose reddish timber is prized for furniture. Yellow flowers bloom in cascades across the country every April.

flower.label: National flower
flower.title: Jasminum sambac
flower.desc: A small, fragrant white jasmine. Strung into garlands sold at churches and intersections, used to welcome guests and honor icons.

executive.label: Exec
executive.body: **President** — head of state & government, elected for a single 6-year term. Cabinet of ~24 executive departments.

legislative.label: Leg
legislative.body: **Congress** — bicameral. Senate of 24 elected at-large; House of Representatives with ~316 district & party-list members.

judicial.label: Jud
judicial.body: **Supreme Court** — 15 Justices (1 Chief, 14 Associate). Appointed by the President from the JBC's shortlist.

constitutional.label: Const
constitutional.body: **Constitutional commissions** — Elections (COMELEC), Audit (COA), Civil Service (CSC) — independent bodies.

local.label: LGU
local.body: **Local units** — 18 regions, 82 provinces, 146 cities, 1,488 municipalities, 42,046 barangays.

hero.title: History of the Philippines
hero.description: More than 700,000 years of human story — from the peopling of the archipelago, to Austronesian maritime polities, 333 years of Spanish rule, half a century under the United States, wartime occupation, and the long road to the Fifth Republic.

scholarNote.title: Scholarly note
scholarNote.body: Most of what we know of pre-colonial polities comes from Chinese records, ceramics, and oral traditions; written indigenous archives were rare and largely destroyed in the Spanish era.

entries.title: Earliest human presence
entries.body: Stone tools and butchered rhinoceros bones found in Kalinga, northern Luzon, suggest hominins — possibly Homo erectus — were present in the Philippines some 700,000 years ago. Who exactly they were remains one of the great open questions of Southeast Asian prehistory.

entries.title: Tabon Man
entries.body: Skull fragments discovered in Tabon Cave, Palawan, are the oldest confirmed remains of modern humans in the Philippines. The cave complex shows continuous human occupation for tens of millennia.

entries.title: Laguna Copperplate Inscription
entries.body: The oldest known written document found in the Philippines. Inscribed in Kawi script, it records the forgiveness of a debt of gold and demonstrates Philippine connections to a wider Hindu-Buddhist maritime world. It was recovered near the mouth of the Lumbang River in 1989.

entries.title: Arrival of Islam
entries.body: Makdum Karim, a Muslim missionary, lands in Sulu. Islam spreads through the southern islands, giving rise to the Sultanates of Sulu (1457) and Maguindanao, which would resist Spanish rule for three centuries.

entries.title: Magellan's expedition
entries.body: Ferdinand Magellan, sailing under the Spanish crown, reaches the archipelago and is killed at the Battle of Mactan by warriors led by Lapu-Lapu. The encounter is now commemorated annually as a founding moment of Filipino resistance.

entries.title: Spanish colonization begins
entries.body: Miguel López de Legazpi establishes the first permanent Spanish settlement in Cebu, and by 1571, Manila becomes the capital of the new colony. The islands are named after King Philip II of Spain. Spanish rule will last 333 years.

entries.title: Philippine Revolution
entries.body: The secret society Katipunan, founded by Andrés Bonifacio, launches an armed revolt against Spanish colonial rule. The revolution will produce the first national army, flag, and anthem.

entries.title: Declaration of independence
entries.body: Emilio Aguinaldo proclaims Philippine independence from a window in Kawit, Cavite. The national flag is unfurled for the first time and the Marcha Nacional Filipina (later Lupang Hinirang) is played publicly.

entries.title: Treaty of Paris
entries.body: Spain cedes the Philippines to the United States for $20 million following the Spanish-American War. The Philippine-American War (1899–1902) follows. American rule would last nearly 50 years and shape the country's institutions, education, and English-speaking civil service.

entries.title: Commonwealth established
entries.body: The Tydings-McDuffie Act creates the Commonwealth of the Philippines as a transitional government toward independence. Manuel L. Quezon becomes the first President of the Commonwealth.

entries.title: Japanese occupation
entries.body: Imperial Japan invades and occupies the Philippines for three and a half years. The Bataan Death March (1942) and the Battle of Manila (1945) are among WWII's most harrowing episodes. Guerrilla resistance and the U.S.-Philippine liberation campaign end the occupation.

entries.title: Independence recognized
entries.body: The United States formally grants Philippine independence. Manuel Roxas becomes the first president of the Third Republic. The date of independence will later be moved back to June 12, 1898 by President Diosdado Macapagal in 1962.

entries.title: Marcos declares martial law
entries.body: President Ferdinand Marcos issues Proclamation 1081, placing the entire country under martial law for 14 years. Thousands are detained, tortured, or killed; press freedom is suspended; the 1935 Constitution is replaced. Billions in public funds are diverted.

entries.title: People Power Revolution
entries.body: Millions of Filipinos converge on Epifanio de los Santos Avenue (EDSA) in a peaceful, four-day uprising that topples the Marcos regime. Corazon Aquino is sworn in as President. The revolution inspires democratic movements worldwide and remains a defining moment in Philippine history.

entries.title: Ratification of the 1987 Constitution
entries.body: A new Constitution is overwhelmingly ratified in a national plebiscite. It restores a democratic, presidential system with a Bill of Rights, an independent judiciary, and strict limits on presidential power. It remains the country's supreme law today.

entries.title: Local Government Code
entries.body: Republic Act 7160 devolves significant powers, functions, and revenues from the national government to provinces, cities, municipalities, and barangays — reshaping how public services are delivered and laying the foundation for modern local governance.

entries.title: BARMM established
entries.body: The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) replaces the ARMM after decades of peace talks between the national government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front. It is the country's only autonomous region with a parliamentary form of government.

overview.title: Historical Overview
paragraphs: The Philippines' history spans thousands of years, beginning with the migration of Austronesian peoples. These early settlers developed sophisticated societies, trading with various Asian civilizations and developing unique cultural traditions.

The arrival of Ferdinand Magellan in 1521 marked the beginning of Spanish colonization, which would last for over three centuries. This period saw the widespread adoption of Christianity and the establishment of colonial institutions that would significantly influence Filipino society.

Following the Spanish-American War, the Philippines came under American rule, leading to significant changes in education, governance, and society. The country achieved independence in 1946 and has since worked to build a modern nation while preserving its rich cultural heritage.

regionalOverview.title: Regional Overview
paragraphs: The Philippines is divided into three main geographical divisions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. These are further subdivided into 18 regions, each with its own administrative center, cultural identity, and economic focus.

Each region showcases unique traditions, dialects, and cuisines, contributing to the country's rich cultural tapestry. From the mountain tribes of the Cordilleras to the seafaring communities of the Visayas, the diversity of Filipino regional cultures is remarkable.

The regions also vary in their economic activities, from the industrial and service-oriented National Capital Region to the agricultural heartlands of Central Luzon and the resource-rich provinces of Mindanao.
